questions.questionText: What percentage of a cell's mass is made up of water?
questions.hint: Water is the most abundant substance in living organisms.
questions.explanation: Water makes up approximately 70-95% of a cell's mass depending on cell type.

questions.questionText: What type of bond holds water molecules together?
questions.hint: Weak bonds between adjacent water molecules.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds form between the hydrogen of one water molecule and the oxygen of another.

questions.questionText: Which property of water allows it to act as a solvent?
questions.hint: Like dissolves like - water dissolves polar substances.
questions.explanation: Water's polar nature allows it to dissolve ionic and polar compounds, making it an excellent solvent.

questions.questionText: Which mineral ion is essential for nerve impulse transmission?
questions.hint: Key for action potentials in neurons.
questions.explanation: Sodium ions are critical for generating action potentials in nerve cells.

questions.questionText: What is cohesion in water?
questions.hint: Attraction between water molecules themselves.
questions.explanation: Cohesion is the attraction between water molecules due to hydrogen bonding.

questions.questionText: Which element is needed for the formation of hemoglobin?
questions.hint: Carries oxygen in blood.
questions.explanation: Iron is the central atom in the heme group of hemoglobin, which binds oxygen.

questions.questionText: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
questions.hint: Midpoint on the pH scale.
questions.explanation: A pH of 7 is neutral (neither acidic nor basic), such as pure water at 25°C.

questions.questionText: Which property of water helps regulate body temperature?
questions.hint: Water absorbs and releases heat slowly.
questions.explanation: Water's high specific heat capacity means it absorbs or loses much heat before changing temperature, helping stabilize body temperature.

questions.questionText: Which buffer system maintains blood pH near 7.4?
questions.hint: Involves CO2 and H2O.
questions.explanation: The carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer system maintains blood pH through the equilibrium: H2O + CO2 ⇌ H2CO3 ⇌ H+ + HCO3-.

questions.questionText: Which mineral is the major component of bone and teeth?
questions.hint: Most abundant mineral in the human body.
questions.explanation: Calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite) makes up the mineral matrix of bones and teeth.

questions.questionText: What happens to water's density when it freezes?
questions.hint: Think about ice floating on water.
questions.explanation: Ice is less dense than liquid water because hydrogen bonding causes molecules to form a lattice structure with more space between them.

questions.questionText: Which ion is critical for muscle contraction?
questions.hint: Released from sarcoplasmic reticulum.
questions.explanation: Calcium ions trigger muscle contraction by binding to troponin and exposing myosin-binding sites on actin.

questions.questionText: What is the role of iodine in the human body?
questions.hint: Deficiency causes goitre.
questions.explanation: Iodine is an essential component of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) which regulate metabolism.

questions.questionText: Which mineral is essential for chlorophyll in plants?
questions.hint: Central atom in the chlorophyll molecule.
questions.explanation: Magnesium is at the centre of the porphyrin ring in chlorophyll, analogous to iron in haemoglobin.

questions.questionText: Why does sweating help cool the body?

options.text: Sweat absorbs heat from the skin
Latent heat of vaporisation is absorbed from the skin

questions.hint: Phase change requires energy.
questions.explanation: When sweat evaporates, it absorbs latent heat of vaporisation from the skin, cooling the body.

questions.questionText: Which statement about capillary action in plants is correct?

options.text: It is caused by cohesion and adhesion of water molecules
It is caused by gravity pulling water downwards
It requires active transport of water
It only works in tall trees over 50m

questions.hint: Uptake of water against gravity.
questions.explanation: Capillary action results from cohesion (water sticking to itself) and adhesion (water sticking to xylem walls), combined with surface tension.

questions.questionText: What is the role of bicarbonate (HCO3-) in human physiology?
questions.hint: Part of the carbonic acid-bicarbonate buffer.
questions.explanation: Bicarbonate ions accept H+ ions to form carbonic acid, buffering blood pH within the narrow range of 7.35-7.45.

questions.questionText: A solution with a pH of 3 is how many times more acidic than a solution with pH of 5?
questions.hint: pH scale is logarithmic.
questions.explanation: Each pH unit represents a 10-fold difference in H+ concentration. A difference of 2 units = 10 × 10 = 100 times more acidic.

questions.questionText: Why does ice float on water despite being made of the same molecule?

options.text: Hydrogen bonding creates a crystalline lattice with more space
Ice has a lower molecular weight
Water molecules move faster in ice

questions.hint: Think about the structure formed when water freezes.
questions.explanation: When water freezes, hydrogen bonds arrange molecules in a crystalline lattice with open spaces, making ice less dense than liquid water.

questions.questionText: In a hyperosmotic solution, what happens to an animal cell?

options.text: Water moves into the cell and it bursts
Water moves out of the cell and it shrivels
Ions move into the cell by diffusion

questions.hint: Hyperosmotic means higher solute concentration outside.
questions.explanation: In a hyperosmotic solution (higher solute concentration outside), water moves out of the cell by osmosis, causing the cell to shrivel (crenation).
